categories.name: Fast ER Triage & Minimal Diagnostics
categories.description: Short, rapid cases that conclude immediately at triage or with basic lab tests (Leucocytes/CRP) within minutes and without hospitalization or intensive interventions.
categories.rationale: Grounded in variants like V0001, V0002, V0003, and V0292, which show extremely short durations (minutes) and very low trace lengths ending in triage or quick lab results.

categories.name: Acute ER Care with IV Intervention
categories.description: Standard acute sepsis care pathways involving triage, comprehensive blood work (CRP, Leucocytes, LacticAcid), and administration of intravenous liquids and antibiotics within a short duration.
categories.rationale: Grounded in frequent variants like V0004, V0005, V0006, V0007, and V0009, which feature standard diagnostic panels followed by IV therapy within hours.

categories.name: Standard Hospital Admission and Release
categories.description: Cases requiring formal hospital admission (Admission NC or Admission IC) followed by a standard inpatient stay and subsequent discharge (Release A, B, C, or D).
categories.rationale: Grounded in variants that incorporate ward admissions and end in regular release outcomes over a span of days, such as V0008, V0068, and V0070.

categories.name: Chronic Rework and Readmission
categories.description: Extreme outliers characterized by extensive loops, highly repeated lab tests (CRP, LacticAcid, Leucocytes) and ward admissions, spanning multiple months and frequently culminating in returns to the ER or prolonged stays.
categories.rationale: Grounded in extremely long and complex variants like V0317, V0551, V0605, V0625, and V0710, where extensive rework and long durations dominate the process profile.
